description: todolist v1: a multi-tenant todolist app (organizations, projects, lists, items) with per-project and per-list ACLs, AI agents that use lists over MCP, an audit log, and a React UI with Google login. Stack and domain decisions are in DECISIONS.md; README.md lists the v1 features.

userStories.title: Backend scaffold
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a FastAPI project managed by uv with linting, type checking and tests so that every later story starts from working quality checks.
acceptanceCriteria: pyproject.toml at the repo root, managed by uv, requires-python >= 3.14, package in src/todolist/
FastAPI app factory create_app() in src/todolist/app.py; GET /healthz returns 200 {"status": "ok"}
Settings class based on pydantic-settings reading from environment and .env; .env is git-ignored and .env.example is committed
ruff (lint + format) and pyright (strict mode for src/) configured in pyproject.toml
pytest with pytest-asyncio and an httpx AsyncClient fixture; a test covers /healthz
.gitignore covers .venv, __pycache__, .env, node_modules, frontend/dist
Root CLAUDE.md lists the run command (uv run uvicorn ...) and the quality check commands
uv run ruff check and uv run ruff format --check pass
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy and Alembic
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a Postgres database with async SQLAlchemy sessions and migrations so that models can be added story by story.
acceptanceCriteria: docker-compose.yml with a postgres:18 service, a named volume and a healthcheck; it provides two databases: todolist (dev) and todolist_test
DATABASE_URL and TEST_DATABASE_URL settings with defaults that match docker compose, documented in .env.example
Async engine and session factory (SQLAlchemy 2 + asyncpg) and a get_session FastAPI dependency in src/todolist/db.py
Declarative Base with a naming convention for constraints; shared mixins for a UUID primary key and created_at / updated_at
Alembic configured for the async engine with autogenerate against Base.metadata; uv run alembic upgrade head works on an empty database
Test fixtures: schema is migrated once per session on todolist_test, each test runs in a transaction that is rolled back, and the app's get_session is overridden to use it
A test proves isolation: a row inserted in one test is not visible in the next
Root CLAUDE.md documents docker compose up -d and the alembic commands
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: User, Organization and Membership models
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to store users, organizations and memberships so that every other feature can be scoped to an organization.
acceptanceCriteria: users table: id, email (unique, stored lowercased), name, avatar_url nullable, google_sub nullable unique, timestamps
organizations table: id, name, slug (unique), timestamps
memberships table: id, organization_id, user_id, role enum owner | admin | member, unique (organization_id, user_id), cascade delete with the organization
Alembic migration generated and applied; alembic upgrade head followed by alembic downgrade base works
Tests cover creating a user with an organization and membership, and the unique constraints
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Sessions, dev-login and default organization
userStories.description: As a new user, I want to be signed in with a session and get a default organization automatically so that I can start without setting anything up.
acceptanceCriteria: Signed cookie session (Starlette SessionMiddleware, SESSION_SECRET setting, httponly, samesite=lax, secure outside dev)
Service function get_or_create_user(email, name, google_sub=None): on first creation it also creates a default organization named "<name>'s organization" with a unique slug and an owner membership
current_user dependency returns the session's user or raises 401 with a JSON error body
POST /api/auth/dev-login {email, name} signs in through get_or_create_user; it returns 404 unless the DEV_LOGIN setting is true (default false)
POST /api/auth/logout clears the session; GET /api/me returns the user plus their organizations with role
GET /api/config returns {dev_login_enabled, google_login_enabled} without authentication
Tests cover: first login creates exactly one default organization, second login creates none, /api/me returns 401 when signed out, dev-login returns 404 when disabled
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Google OAuth login
userStories.description: As a user, I want to sign in with my Google account so that I do not need a separate password.
acceptanceCriteria: Authlib OpenID Connect client for Google configured from GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET settings (documented in .env.example); google_login_enabled in /api/config is true only when both are set
GET /api/auth/google/login redirects to Google with state; an optional next parameter (relative paths only) is kept in the session
GET /api/auth/google/callback validates state, reads email, name, picture and sub from the ID token, rejects unverified emails, signs in through get_or_create_user and redirects to next or /
An existing user with the same email and no google_sub is linked instead of duplicated
Both endpoints return 404 when Google login is not configured
Tests mock the Google token exchange and cover: new user, returning user, unverified email rejected, absolute next URL ignored
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: No real Google credentials are available to the loop. Never call Google in tests.

userStories.title: Organization API

POST /api/orgs {name} creates an organization with a unique slug and makes the creator owner
GET /api/orgs/{org_id} returns the organization for members; non-members get 404
PATCH /api/orgs/{org_id} {name} is allowed for owner and admin; member gets 403
A reusable dependency resolves the organization and the caller's membership for all org-scoped routes

DELETE /api/orgs/{org_id}/members/{user_id} is allowed for owner and admin; a member can remove themselves (leave)

POST /api/orgs/{org_id}/invitations {email, role} for owner and admin: if a user with that email exists they are added as a member immediately, otherwise an invitation is stored; inviting an existing member returns 409
GET /api/orgs/{org_id}/invitations lists pending invitations; DELETE /api/orgs/{org_id}/invitations/{id} revokes one
get_or_create_user converts all pending invitations for the email into memberships on sign-in (the invited user still gets their own default organization)

userStories.title: Agent model and API
userStories.description: As an organization admin, I want to register AI agents in my organization so that they can be given access to projects and lists.

GET /api/orgs/{org_id}/agents lists agents for any member
POST /api/orgs/{org_id}/agents {name, description}, PATCH and DELETE /api/orgs/{org_id}/agents/{agent_id} are allowed for owner and admin only
A Principal value type (kind: user | agent, id, organization context) is introduced in src/todolist and documented in DECISIONS.md as the actor type for permissions and audit

userStories.title: Project model and API
userStories.description: As an organization member, I want to create projects in an organization so that I can group related lists.
acceptanceCriteria: projects table: id, organization_id, name, description nullable, created_by, timestamps, cascade delete with the organization; migration applied
POST /api/orgs/{org_id}/projects {name, description} is allowed for any organization member

GET /api/orgs/{org_id}/projects, GET /api/projects/{project_id}, PATCH /api/projects/{project_id}, DELETE /api/projects/{project_id} exist and are limited to organization members for now (ACL comes in US-011)
Non-members get 404 on every project route
Tests cover CRUD and the non-member case
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Project ACL and permission service
userStories.description: As a project admin, I want access to a project to be limited to the people and agents it was shared with so that projects in one organization can be private.
acceptanceCriteria: project_grants table: id, project_id, principal_kind user | agent, user_id nullable, agent_id nullable, role viewer | editor | admin, check constraint that exactly one of user_id / agent_id matches principal_kind, unique per project and principal; migration applied
Permission service in src/todolist/permissions.py: effective_project_role(principal, project) returns admin for organization owners and admins, otherwise the grant's role, otherwise None
Creating a project grants its creator the admin role
Project routes are enforced: no role gives 404; GET needs viewer; PATCH needs editor; DELETE needs admin; the project list returns only projects where the caller has a role
A reusable dependency (for example require_project_role("editor")) is used by the routes and documented in ralph/progress.txt Codebase Patterns
Tests cover the matrix of organization owner, org member with each grant role and org member without a grant
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: effective_project_role takes the database session as its first argument: effective_project_role(session, principal, project).

userStories.title: Project grants API
userStories.description: As a project admin, I want to share a project with users and agents and choose their role so that I control who can see and change it.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/projects/{project_id}/grants lists grants with principal kind, id, display name and role (project admin only)
PUT /api/projects/{project_id}/grants {principal_kind, principal_id, role} creates or updates a grant; the principal must be a member or an agent of the project's organization (422 otherwise)
DELETE /api/projects/{project_id}/grants/{grant_id} revokes a grant
The last admin grant on a project cannot be removed or downgraded when no organization owner or admin remains able to administer it (409)
Tests cover granting to a user, granting to an agent, updating, revoking, a principal from another organization, and non-admin callers (403)
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: List model and API with mode
userStories.description: As a project editor, I want to create lists in a project and mark each as human-only, AI-only or mixed so that it is clear who works on it.
acceptanceCriteria: todo_lists table: id, project_id, name, description nullable, mode enum human_only | ai_only | mixed, position, created_by, timestamps, cascade delete with the project; migration applied
POST /api/projects/{project_id}/lists {name, description, mode?} needs project editor; when mode is omitted it defaults to mixed if the organization has at least one agent, otherwise human_only
GET /api/projects/{project_id}/lists (viewer), GET /api/lists/{list_id} (viewer), PATCH /api/lists/{list_id} for name, description and mode (editor), DELETE /api/lists/{list_id} (admin)
Access uses the project role for now (list-level ACL comes in US-014)
Tests cover CRUD, both default-mode cases, explicit mode and the role requirements
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: List ACL
userStories.description: As a list admin, I want to give a user or agent a different role on one list than on the rest of the project so that access can be set per list.
acceptanceCriteria: list_grants table with the same shape as project_grants but with list_id and role none | viewer | editor | admin (none hides the list from that principal); migration applied
effective_list_role(principal, todo_list): organization owners and admins get admin; otherwise the list grant if one exists (none means no access); otherwise the project role
A principal with a list grant but no project grant can open that list directly and sees the parent project name, but not the project's other lists
List routes use effective_list_role; the list index of a project returns only lists the caller can see
GET, PUT and DELETE on /api/lists/{list_id}/grants mirror the project grants API and need list admin
Tests cover: override up (project viewer, list editor), override down (project editor, list viewer), none, list-only access, organization admin
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Item model and API
userStories.description: As a list editor, I want to add, edit, complete and delete items so that I can track what has to be done.
acceptanceCriteria: items table: id, list_id, title, notes nullable, status enum open | done, position, created_by_kind + created_by_id, completed_by_kind + completed_by_id nullable, completed_at nullable, timestamps, cascade delete with the list; migration applied
Item operations live in a service module (src/todolist/services/items.py or similar) that takes a Principal, so the HTTP API and the MCP tools can share them
GET /api/lists/{list_id}/items returns items ordered by position (viewer); POST /api/lists/{list_id}/items {title, notes} appends at the end (editor)
PATCH /api/items/{item_id} updates title, notes and status (editor); setting status to done records completed_by and completed_at, reopening clears them
DELETE /api/items/{item_id} (editor)
Tests cover CRUD, complete and reopen, ordering and the viewer-cannot-write case
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Item reordering
userStories.description: As a list editor, I want to move items up and down so that the list reflects my priorities.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/items/{item_id}/move {before_item_id | null} moves the item before the given item of the same list, or to the end when null (editor)
Positions stay unique and gap-free within a list after any move, create or delete
Moving before an item of another list returns 422
The move is a service function that takes a Principal
Tests cover move to start, middle and end, and the cross-list case
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: List mode enforcement
userStories.description: As a list owner, I want the human-only / AI-only / mixed mode to be enforced so that agents stay out of human lists and humans do not change AI lists by accident.
acceptanceCriteria: The permission service exposes one check used by all item and list operations, combining effective_list_role with the list mode and the principal kind
human_only: agent principals have no access (the list is invisible to them) regardless of grants

ai_only: user principals keep read access according to their role but cannot create, edit, complete, move or delete items (403 with a clear error code such as list_ai_only); list admins can still change the list's name, mode and grants
mixed: both kinds act according to their role
Service-level tests use an agent Principal directly (no MCP needed yet) and cover all three modes for both principal kinds
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Audit event recording
userStories.description: As a project admin, I want every change to be recorded with who did it so that I can trace what humans and agents changed.
acceptanceCriteria: audit_events table: id, organization_id, project_id nullable, list_id nullable, actor_kind user | agent, actor_id, actor_name (snapshot), action (dotted string such as item.completed), target_kind, target_id, details JSONB, created_at; indexes on (project_id, created_at) and (list_id, created_at); events survive deletion of their target (no cascading foreign keys on project_id / list_id / target_id); migration applied
record_event(session, principal, action, ...) writes in the caller's transaction, so an event exists only if the change committed

Events are recorded for: project created / updated / deleted; list created / updated (including mode change with old and new value) / deleted; item created / updated / completed / reopened / moved / deleted; project and list grant set / revoked
details holds changed fields with old and new values for updates
Tests assert the event for each action and that a failed request records nothing
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Audit log API
userStories.description: As a project or list admin, I want to read the audit log per project and per list so that I can review activity.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/projects/{project_id}/audit returns the project's events, including events of its lists and items, newest first (project admin only)
GET /api/lists/{list_id}/audit returns the list's events, including its items (list admin only)
Cursor pagination (limit default 50, max 200, next_cursor in the response)
Optional filters: actor_kind, actor_id, action prefix (for example item.)
Tests cover scoping (events of another list are not returned), pagination, filters and the 403 for non-admins
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: OAuth server: storage, metadata and client registration
userStories.description: As an MCP client, I need to discover the authorization server and register myself so that I can start an OAuth flow without manual configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: Add the official mcp Python SDK as a dependency and read its current documentation on authorization before designing; record in DECISIONS.md whether the SDK's authorization-server provider interface is used or the endpoints are hand-written

Tables for oauth_clients (client_id, hashed secret nullable, redirect_uris, client_name, grant types, created_at), oauth_authorization_codes, oauth_access_tokens and oauth_refresh_tokens (tokens stored hashed, with agent_id, user_id, client_id, scope, expires_at, revoked_at); migration applied

PUBLIC_BASE_URL setting; GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server returns RFC 8414 metadata (issuer, authorization, token, registration and revocation endpoints, S256 as the only code challenge method)
GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (and the /mcp-suffixed variant if the current MCP spec requires it) returns RFC 9728 metadata pointing at this authorization server
POST /register implements dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) for public clients; redirect URIs must be https or loopback http
Tests cover both metadata documents and registration including an invalid redirect URI
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Check the current MCP authorization spec revision; do not rely on memory for endpoint names and required metadata fields. Done against MCP spec revision 2026-07-28 and mcp SDK 2.3.0; endpoints are hand-written (DECISIONS.md).

userStories.title: OAuth authorize endpoint and consent API
userStories.description: As a user, I want to approve an MCP client and choose which agent it acts as so that an AI tool gets exactly that agent's access.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /authorize validates client_id, redirect_uri (exact match), response_type=code, code_challenge with S256 and state; invalid client or redirect URI shows an error instead of redirecting
When the user has no session, /authorize redirects to the login page with a next parameter that returns to the same authorize URL
With a session, /authorize stores a pending authorization request (short-lived, server-side) and redirects to the SPA route /oauth/consent?request=<id>
GET /api/oauth/requests/{id} returns the client name, redirect host and the agents the user may choose (agents of organizations where the user is owner or admin)

POST /api/oauth/requests/{id}/approve {agent_id} issues a single-use authorization code (10 minute expiry) bound to client, redirect_uri, code challenge, user and agent, and returns the redirect URL with code and state; POST .../deny returns the redirect URL with error=access_denied
A user cannot approve for an agent of an organization they do not administer (403)
Tests cover the happy path, missing PKCE, mismatched redirect_uri, unauthenticated redirect, deny and the forbidden agent
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The consent page itself is built in US-037; this story delivers the backend only. Done: `state` is optional (the MCP spec makes it a SHOULD for clients) and returned unchanged when sent; every authorization response also carries `iss` (RFC 9207). An agent the user may not authorize is a 403 whether or not it exists.

userStories.title: OAuth token endpoint
userStories.description: As an MCP client, I need to exchange a code for tokens and refresh them so that I can call the MCP server over time.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /token with grant_type=authorization_code verifies the code, client, redirect_uri and PKCE verifier, marks the code used and returns an access token (1 hour) and a refresh token
Reusing an authorization code fails and revokes the tokens issued from it
grant_type=refresh_token rotates the refresh token and issues a new access token; a reused refresh token is rejected
POST /revoke (RFC 7009) revokes an access or refresh token
A function resolve_access_token(token) returns the agent Principal for a valid token, and None for expired, revoked or unknown tokens or when the agent was deleted
Error responses follow RFC 6749 (invalid_grant, invalid_client, unsupported_grant_type)
Tests cover exchange, wrong verifier, code reuse, refresh rotation, revocation and expiry
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: MCP server with bearer authentication
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to connect to the app's MCP endpoint with my token so that I can use the lists I was given access to.
acceptanceCriteria: An MCP server built with the official mcp SDK is mounted in the FastAPI app at /mcp using the streamable HTTP transport; the app lifespan starts and stops it correctly
Requests without a valid bearer token get 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header that points to the protected resource metadata, as the current MCP authorization spec requires
A valid token resolves to the agent Principal through resolve_access_token and is available inside tool handlers together with a database session
Tool whoami returns the agent's name, its organization and the number of lists it can access
Tests use the SDK's client against the ASGI app (no network): unauthenticated is rejected, authenticated whoami returns the agent
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: MCP read tools
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to discover projects and lists and read their items so that I know what work exists.
acceptanceCriteria: Tool list_projects returns the projects in which the agent can see at least one list (id, name, description)
Tool list_lists(project_id?) returns the lists the agent can access with id, name, mode, project, the agent's role and open / done item counts; human_only lists never appear
Tool get_list(list_id, include_done=false) returns the list and its items in position order
Every tool has a description and typed parameters that explain usage to a model; unknown or inaccessible ids return a clear tool error, not a stack trace
All tools go through the permission service with the agent Principal
Tests cover visibility by grant, the human_only exclusion and the error for an inaccessible list
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: MCP write tools
userStories.description: As an AI agent, I want to add, update, complete and delete items so that I can work a list on my own.
acceptanceCriteria: Tools add_item(list_id, title, notes?), update_item(item_id, title?, notes?), complete_item(item_id), reopen_item(item_id), move_item(item_id, before_item_id?) and delete_item(item_id)
The tools call the same item service functions as the HTTP API; no item logic is duplicated
The agent needs the editor role on the list; a viewer agent gets a clear permission error
Each change records an audit event with actor_kind agent

Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: End-to-end MCP OAuth test
userStories.description: As a developer, I want one test that walks the complete agent onboarding flow so that regressions in the OAuth and MCP chain are caught.
acceptanceCriteria: A single integration test runs against the ASGI app: discover metadata, register a client, sign in a user (dev-login), authorize with PKCE, approve for an agent, exchange the code, connect with the SDK's MCP client, add and complete an item, refresh the token, call a tool again, revoke, and confirm the next call is rejected
The test asserts the resulting item state through the HTTP API as the human user and asserts the audit log entries
Any defect found in US-020 to US-025 while writing this test is fixed in this story
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The test (tests/test_mcp_oauth_e2e.py) drives the flow with the SDK's own OAuthClientProvider and Client. It found no defect in US-020 to US-025.

userStories.title: Frontend scaffold

userStories.title: API client, login page and auth guard

userStories.title: Organization settings page
userStories.description: As an organization owner, I want to rename my organization and manage members and invitations in the UI.

userStories.title: Projects in the UI
userStories.description: As a user, I want to create, open, rename and delete projects in the UI.
acceptanceCriteria: "New project" action in the sidebar opens a dialog (name, description) and navigates to the new project
